capability: Small-strain radial paired-node conductivity and fixed-initial-mass lumped nodal heat capacity with temperature-dependent specific heat
acceptance: Ten complete production increments cover nonuniform heating with variable k/rho/cp, a temperature-and-geometry hold, and a volumetric-source ramp. Source amplitudes use the same interval-average time evaluation as native Abaqus. Each thermal operator uses reference geometry. Forty native HFL samples are retained only as a nodal-reconstruction diagnostic because production body heat flux is not exported.

capability: Finite-strain radial midpoint conduction, fixed-initial-mass nodal capacity and current-geometry source with variable conductivity and specific heat
acceptance: User-authorized case-specific tolerance qualification; exact current gates and scope in verification/abaqus/2025/tolerance_qualification.md. Historical gate descriptions below do not override this qualification. Ten complete native and production increments combine nonuniform temperature, two nonproportional diagonal deformation stages, a hold and source activation. Midpoint radial gradients and reference quadrature fractions times whole current volume determine conduction; reference initial mass determines nodal capacity, while actual pointwise current volume determines source weights. The native thermal-capacity comparison is retained as a separate discretization check. All paired heat reactions, actual heat-rate diagnostics and isolated node source increments retain three relative metric gates below 0.1 percent with separate exact-zero and balance gates. Existing stress, elastic, displacement, reaction, axial-resultant and energy checks remain; hold-stage zero elastic-energy increments are checked absolutely. Native HFL remains explicitly diagnostic, reconstructed from exported nodal histories rather than compared with an unavailable production flux field.

capability: Finite radial paired-endpoint material temperature with temperature-dependent Young modulus and mean thermal expansion
acceptance: User-authorized case-specific tolerance qualification; exact current gates and scope in verification/abaqus/2025/tolerance_qualification.md. Ten prescribed nonproportional finite-strain production increments compare all 40 native nodal and 40 material-point samples using the complete nonuniform thermal-mechanical checker. Temperature, displacement, stress and elastic tensors, both radial reactions, both end reactions, axial section force/strain and mechanical elastic-energy changes require all three relative metrics below 0.1 percent. Native Poisson ratio is constant 0.3; temperature-dependent Poisson ratio and small-strain branches are covered independently by local tests. All 20 paired radial heat reactions and ten actual stored/generated/Dirichlet heat rates are also compared below 0.1 percent, with separate balance and zero gates. capability: CAX4T paired-corner temperature for elastic, plastic and Norton parameters
acceptance: Eight production runs compare every accepted increment and all four nodes/material points against unchanged native CSVs: temperature, nonzero displacement and normal stress/elastic/plastic/creep components, equivalent histories and their increments require relative L2, relative absolute peak and maximum pointwise errors below 0.1 percent. capability: Finite-strain C3D8RT fuel-plate bending and axial extension with fully coupled J2 plasticity and Norton creep, compared with Abaqus for accuracy and single-core timing
acceptance: The matched 1785-node, 1200-element, 7140-degree-of-freedom path uses five fixed two-second increments, a 600 to 800 kelvin front-face ramp, a 600 kelvin back face, a 0.8 millimetre axial extension, the same heat source, finite-strain C3D8RT formulation, and clamp in both solvers. Both regions use the same fixed 1 MPa initial yield stress, 20 GPa linear isotropic hardening, and Norton rate of 3.5e-4 per second at 100 MPa with exponent 3; these simplified constants exercise the path and are not empirical fuel or cladding models. The five snapshots compare 8925 nodal rows, 6000 one-point C3D8RT material-integration rows, and 5 energy rows. All 6000 material-point rows have nonzero plastic and creep references. Maximum equivalent plastic and creep strains are 0.00802400 and 0.00823199. Reaction-force, stress, elastic-strain, plastic-strain, creep-strain, equivalent-history, nodal, and energy quantities all pass relative L2, relative absolute-peak, and maximum pointwise relative gates of 0.5 percent without a denominator floor; the largest accepted pointwise value is 0.447050 percent for the reaction-force vector. Fuelsim completes with 26 nonlinear iterations, 26 Jacobian evaluations, and one PETSc workspace; Abaqus uses 14 nonlinear iterations and 14 matrix decompositions. With CPU 0 pinned, MUMPS, all numerical-library threads fixed to one, and output disabled, Fuelsim production-entry external samples are 5.30, 5.34, and 5.34 seconds with a 5.34-second median; Abaqus cpus=1 samples are 5.389362, 5.4808106, and 5.3975893 seconds with a 5.3975893-second median. Fuelsim uses 1.06694 percent less wall time. The same physical workload through the production entry at pre-change commit 26dde87, using its default SCOTCH ordering, has a 5.88-second median; the current PORD-selected path is 9.18367 percent lower while the material and load parameters remain fixed. This overall value includes ordering and line-search selections. Forcing PORD on both commits gives 5.35 and 5.34 second medians, isolating a 0.186916 percent reduction from the C++ assembly and data-path changes.

capability: Steady-state finite-strain C3D8RT fuel-plate thermoelastic final-equilibrium comparison with Abaqus
acceptance: The exact 1785-node, 1200-element, 7140-degree-of-freedom comparison uses one Fuelsim steady load step and one Abaqus steady-state coupled temperature-displacement increment with the same finite-strain C3D8RT mesh, final 700 and 600 kelvin face temperatures, 2e8 watts per cubic metre fuel heat source, materials, and clamp. Heat capacity is absent from both steady equations. Centered directional differences at all 11 original Newton states give a worst field-block Jacobian error of 8.63e-7, identifying the zero-displacement full-load initial guess rather than a tangent defect as the cause of the excess iterations. A one-iteration small-strain predictor followed by four finite-strain corrector iterations reuses one PETSc workspace. Fuelsim therefore uses 5 nonlinear iterations and 5 Jacobian evaluations, matching Abaqus at 5 nonlinear iterations, 5 equation-solver passes, and 5 matrix decompositions. Temperature relative L2, relative absolute-peak, and maximum pointwise-relative errors are 2.38862e-5, 0.000108914, and 0.000111674 percent. The free-node complete displacement-vector metrics are 0.0126146, 0.0126317, and 0.0485431 percent, all below 0.5 percent without a denominator floor; its maximum absolute difference is 5.75351e-7 metres. Raw Cartesian component pointwise percentages remain diagnostic. Timing files retain three fixed-CPU observations but support no cross-operating-system steady performance claim. This qualifies the one-step steady final equilibrium, not a transient or general path-dependent material response.

capability: Full-size high-heat-flow M5.8 C3D20T finite-strain transient accuracy and single-core timing comparison with Coulomb friction on explicit finite-sliding surface-to-surface mechanical contact
acceptance: The exact 1152-element, 19524-degree-of-freedom B5.51 path adds only the original M5.8 Coulomb coefficient 0.002; both solvers use finite-sliding surface-to-surface contact and zero frictional heat conversion. The revised curved HEX20 path uses one current-geometry constraint and friction history per unique secondary quadratic node, reducing contact contributions from 141568 to 2592 while retaining complete primary-surface candidate sparsity. All 416 secondary contact nodes are projected and sliding. Corner temperature, recovered pressure, constraint gap and pressure, normal-force magnitude, tangential-force magnitude, dominant axial shear, slip magnitude, axial slip, equivalent stress, equivalent plastic strain, equivalent creep strain, recovered pressure integral, and recovered heat integral pass their relative L2, relative absolute-peak, and maximum pointwise-relative gates below 0.5 percent. The complete tangential resultant differs by 0.00225030 percent and 5.02922e-7 newtons, below its explicit 1e-6 newton absolute gate. Radial displacement has 0.00406950 percent relative L2, 0.00631979 percent relative peak, and 0.720715 nanometre maximum absolute error; its pointwise percentage is amplified by near-zero references and remains diagnostic without a denominator floor. The raw three-component tangential nodal-force vector has 0.504191 percent relative L2 because tiny radial and circumferential recovery components use unstable curved bases; its magnitude, axial component, and resultant are the same-physics acceptance quantities. The 7.33773 percent recovered-shear integral compares a constraint resultant with Abaqus smoothed CSHEAR and is also diagnostic. The production executable supplies the final Exodus fields directly to the comparator. MUMPS with automatic/PORD ordering factors a separate numerically equal matrix with exact off-diagonal zeros removed; the complete contact candidate assembly graph is retained and every Jacobian update rebuilds symbolic factorization. Explicit SCOTCH and other PETSc ordering choices retain the full-matrix path. All 209 unified tests pass, including bitwise friction-checkpoint replay and one-/two-process field equivalence. Three alternating output-disabled pairs on the same Intel Core i9-13980HX use CPU 0 and one numerical-library thread. Fuelsim production-entry external runs are 191.03, 193.43, and 194.99 seconds, with a 193.43-second median. Abaqus R2018x cpus=1 external runs are 232.874728, 240.817169, and 239.089524 seconds, with a 239.089524-second median. Fuelsim uses 19.0973 percent less external wall time, a 1.23605x speedup. Abaqus analysis wall times are 227, 236, and 234 seconds; analysis CPU times are 218.30, 223.60, and 224.00 seconds. The programs run on Windows (Abaqus) and WSL2 (Fuelsim). No accuracy gate was relaxed for this optimization.

capability: Full-size high-heat-flow M5.8 C3D20T finite-strain transient field and single-core timing comparison with frictionless finite-sliding surface-to-surface mechanical contact
acceptance: The exact 1152-element path has 5969 quadratic displacement nodes, 1617 corner-temperature nodes, and 19524 coupled degrees of freedom. The fuel heat source is 2e8 watts per cubic metre and its piecewise-linear function is averaged exactly over each time interval, matching the Abaqus DFLUX behavior identified by a one-element C3D20T probe. Each curved finite-sliding secondary face now contributes its scalar gap, residual, and Jacobian through its own current local normal before shared-node averaging; no penalty, material coefficient, mesh, or acceptance gate was fitted. Corner-temperature, radial-displacement, equivalent-stress, equivalent-plastic-strain, and equivalent-creep-strain relative L2 errors are 0.00848164, 0.00336854, 0.00683641, 0.00696828, and 0.0108461 percent. Recovered contact-pressure L2, relative absolute-peak, and maximum pointwise-relative errors are 0.00209098, 0.00298428, and 0.00411733 percent. The corresponding Fuelsim and Abaqus recovered-pressure surface integrals are 11.1444564 and 11.1444412 newtons, a 0.000136010 percent error. Direct projection of the Fuelsim and Abaqus native nodal normal-force vectors onto their current radial directions gives 11.1031394 and 11.1031456 newtons, a 0.0000557156 percent error. The separately reported 0.643605 percent difference between the Fuelsim scalar constraint integral and the Abaqus native nodal-force resultant intentionally compares unlike discrete quantities and is diagnostic, not an acceptance field. Correct bilinear interpolation of the four corner-node thermal HFL values on the quadratic current surface gives contact heat rates of 14.3080635 and 14.3429981 watts, a 0.243566 percent error. Fuelsim completes 20 fixed steps without rejection using 86 nonlinear iterations, 106 residual evaluations, 38 Jacobian evaluations, and one workspace setup. With one numerical-library thread pinned to CPU 0, Fuelsim takes 317.07 seconds externally and 300.873 seconds internally; Abaqus cpus=1 takes 608.050095 seconds externally and reports 604 seconds of analysis time.
